exposure: time spent in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 519 children (160 preterm infants) from the Norwegian Microbiota Study (NoMIC).
finding: Preterm infants had significantly lower bacterial diversity and distinct gut microbiome composition and function in the early postnatal period compared to term infants, which was not explained by common factors like breastfeeding duration, antibiotic exposure, or caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The distinct microbiome composition in preterm infants was not explained by caesarean delivery, and vaginally born, exclusively breastfed preterm infants not exposed to antibiotics still had fewer Firmicutes and more Proteobacteria compared to term infants.
gest_age: Preterm infants and infants born at term were included.
